notes: A lost vision job is now resubmitted instead of waited on forever. The photo-reading endpoint could get into a state the app misread as patience being a virtue: workers crash-loop on boot, one of them takes the queued job down with it, RunPod never requeues it, and then a fresh worker sits idle next to a job the platform has forgotten — while the app extended its wait two minutes at a time, up to fifteen. The poll now recognizes that exact signature (idle or ready workers, nothing initializing or running, queue and in-progress both zero, job still unfinished, twice in a row) and cancels-and-resubmits the job once — an idle worker takes the fresh submission in seconds. If the same thing happens to the resubmission the wait ends with a diagnosis naming the crash-looping worker instead of a shrug, and the extend log line now prints ready and in-progress counts so this state is visible rather than looking like queued=0 with no explanation. The LoRA volume installer got the same medicine from the other night's logs: its pods finished downloading in minutes but their self-delete quietly failed, so the app stared at a done pod for the full twelve-minute clock. It now probes the volume every minute during the wait and deletes the pod itself the moment every file has landed, and the pod script's fallback sleep dropped from ten minutes to one.
